content.text: {"title":"Scaled dot-product scores","narration":"Attention starts by asking: how well does each query match each key? Here is a tiny example with two queries and two keys, each of dimension four, so d k is four. Look at the first [[q]]query, one, zero, one, zero. Take its dot product with the first [[k]]key, one, one, one, one. Multiply matching entries and add them up: that gives two. Doing this for every pair is just the matrix product of Q times K transpose, and it fills the [[s]]score matrix. Now the scaling. The dot products grow with d k, which pushes softmax into flat, tiny-gradient regions. So we [[div]]divide every score by the square root of d k, which here is two. Our two becomes one. The [[sc]]scaled scores are ready for the softmax, which comes next.","objects":[{"kind":"matrix","id":"q","x":120,"y":300,"rows":[["1","0","1","0"],["0","1","1","1"]],"label":"Q"},{"kind":"matrix","id":"k","x":520,"y":300,"rows":[["1","1","1","1"],["1","0","0","1"]],"label":"K"},{"kind":"matrix","id":"s","x":920,"y":300,"rows":[["2","1"],["3","1"]],"label":"Q K transpose","hidden":true},{"kind":"matrix","id":"sc","x":1240,"y":300,"rows":[["1","0.5"],["1.5","0.5"]],"label":"divided by 2","hidden":true},{"kind":"latex","id":"f","x":800,"y":120,"tex":"\\frac{QK^T}{\\sqrt{d_k}},\\ d_k=4"},{"kind":"latex","id":"dot","x":500,"y":600,"tex":"1\\cdot1+0\\cdot1+1\\cdot1+0\\cdot1=2","hidden":true},{"kind":"latex","id":"dv","x":1100,"y":600,"tex":"2/\\sqrt{4}=1","hidden":true}],"actions":[{"do":"highlight","target":{"id":"q","row":0},"durationMs":400,"color":"accent","cue":"q"},{"do":"highlight","target":{"id":"k","row":0},"durationMs":400,"color":"warn","cue":"k"},{"do":"show","target":{"id":"dot"},"durationMs":400,"cue":"k"},{"do":"show","target":{"id":"s"},"durationMs":400,"cue":"s"},{"do":"show","target":{"id":"dv"},"durationMs":400,"cue":"div"},{"do":"show","target":{"id":"sc"},"durationMs":400,"cue":"sc"}],"paperRefs":[{"page":4,"quote":"We compute the dot products of the query with all keys","label":"Section 3.2.1","cue":"k"},{"page":4,"quote":"pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients","cue":"div"}]}
